title: Ascites-derived interleukin-10 drives tumor invasion in advanced epithelial ovarian cancer via STAT3 and ERK1/2 signaling
abstractText: Background: Malignant ascites is a common complication of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC), leading to a considerable decline in patients' quality of life. The objective of this study is to elucidate the source of IL-10 in ascites from advanced EOC patients and investigate the possible underlying mechanisms.Methods: We collected malignant ascites from 21 patients with EOC and determined the IL-10 level by ELISA assay. In vivo studies were performed to assess the potential therapeutic effects of IL-10 antibodies. By flow cytometry and immunomagnetic beads sorting we characterized the regulatory T cells (Tregs) and M2-macrophages in EOC ascites.Finding s: IL-10 level in ascites of advanced EOC patients varied among individuals (134·38±84·80 mmol/L) and displayed a positive correlation with ascites volume (r=0·539, p=0·038) and serum CA125 level (r=0·553, p=0·014). IL-10 in ascites induced EOC cells’ migration and invasion capacity via the phosphorylation of STAT3 and ERK1/2 pathways, both in vitro and in vivo. The percentage of Tregs (3·95±2·07)% and M2-macrophage (12·57±7·78)% in EOC ascites were quantified. Furthermore, Tregs and M2-macrophages, by secreting IL-10, could promote the migration and invasion of EOC cells via the phosphorylation of STAT3 and ERK1/2 pathways.Interpretation : Our findings demonstrate that IL-10 in ascites plays a crucial role in the migration and invasion of EOC cells via the phosphorylation of STAT3 and ERK1/2 pathways. Notably, M2-macrophages and Tregs are two essential sources of IL-10 in EOC ascites.Funding:This study was supported by grants from West China Second University Hospital, Sichuan University (K1518).

title: Novel coupled/BCF models for HCH/DDT flux-bioaccumulation in Zhaotong’s ecological barrier
Sex chromosome turnover as an evolutionary escape from mitonuclear conflict
abstractText: Mitochondrial and nuclear genomes must remain coadapted to sustain oxidative phosphorylation, yet their distinct inheritance often fosters conflict. Sex chromosomes are a key arena for these dynamics: by biasing co-transmission between nuclear-encoded mitochondrial (N-mt) genes and maternally inherited mtDNA, they can amplify or suppress mitonuclear incompatibilities. Existing syntheses emphasize stable XY (mammals) and ZW (birds) systems, where genomic context is conserved. In contrast, many fishes and amphibians undergo frequent shifts among XY, ZW, and polygenic or environmental sex determination, repeatedly resetting the linkage backdrop for mitonuclear interaction. I propose a comparative framework in which sex-chromosome turnover acts as an evolutionary “escape hatch” from Y- or W-linked deleterious N-mt alleles by entrapping N-mt loci into, or releasing them from, non-recombining sex-linked strata, thereby altering the sex bias and intensity of conflict through time. This hypothesis predicts cyclical pulses of hybrid dysfunction and genomic “scars’’ that record historical entrapment, offering testable predictions for when turnover entrenches versus relieves mitonuclear conflict. By integrating evidence from stable and labile vertebrate systems, this article outlines how sex-chromosome dynamics shape mitonuclear coadaptation, postzygotic isolation, and ultimately lineage diversification.

Multi-fidelity predictive model for shock response of energetic materials using conditional U-Net
abstractText: Mapping microstructure to properties is central to materials science. Perhaps most famously, the Hall-Petch relationship relates average grain size to strength. More challenging has been deriving relationships for properties that depend on subtle microstructural features and not average properties. One such example is the initiation of energetic materials under dynamical loading, dominated by energy localization on microstructural features such as pores, cracks, and interfaces. We propose a conditional convolutional neural network to predict the shock-induced temperature field as a function of shock strength, for a wide range of microstructures, and obtained via two different simulation methods. The proposed model, denoted MISTnet2, significantly extends prior work that was limited to a single shock strength, model, and type of microstructure. MISTnet2 can contribute to bridging atomistics with coarse-grain simulations and enable first principles predictions of detonation initiation and safety of this class of materials.

Phase Transition in Binary Compressed Sensing via Annealing with Adaptive Regularization
abstractText: Regularization choice changes the recovery phase diagrams of annealing-based binary compressed sensing. We develop a regularization-selection method that combines systematic parameter search with random forest regression. Under noiseless Gaussian measurements with known sparsity, reference parameters are selected from a candidate grid by minimizing mean squared reconstruction error over repeated simulated annealing (SA) trials. The fitted model predicts these reference values from signal dimension, sampling ratio, and sparsity. With predicted regularization, the SA recovery transition broadly follows the asymptotic reference boundary for box-constrained [Formula: see text] recovery at the larger signal dimensions examined. Without retraining, the same predictor supplies identical regularization values to SA and a quantum–classical hybrid solver. On matched problem instances, the hybrid solver yields smaller mean squared reconstruction errors than SA in parts of the evaluated parameter space. The resulting rule reuses the searched information for subsequent reconstruction without repeating candidate searches at each setting. The results quantify empirical performance under the stated finite candidate grid and solver settings; they do not constitute a solver-independent recovery guarantee or a time-to-solution comparison.

title: Advanced chemical looping-based reverse water–gas shift for methanol production: A techno-economic analysis
abstractText: The transition to a low-carbon economy has driven significant interest in green methanol as a sustainable energy vector and potential platform chemical intermediate; however, the incumbent production pathway via the reverse water-gas shift reaction is hindered by thermodynamic equilibrium limitations and energy-intensive separation steps. This study presents a comparative techno-economic assessment of a novel chemical looping reverse water-gas shift process against the conventional reverse water-gas shift route. Integration of experimental reactor data into rigorous process models demonstrates that the chemical looping pathway overcomes equilibrium constraints, achieving high single-pass carbon dioxide conversion (94% at 650°C) and inherent product separation. This process intensification eliminates the need for syngas recycling, resulting in a reduction of approximately 21% in feedstock requirements and a decrease of 49% in electricity consumption compared to the conventional benchmark. Economically, these technical advantages translate into a net production cost of 2.17 USD per kilogram of methanol, representing a 30% reduction from the 3.12 USD per kilogram estimated for the conventional route. Finally, sensitivity analysis identifies the market price of low-carbon hydrogen as the critical economic driver, revealing that, despite the superior efficiency of the chemical looping design, the commercial viability of both pathways remains fundamentally tied to future reductions in feedstock costs.

title: Fermi-Liquid versus “Strange-Metal” Analyses of the Electrical Resistivity in a Quantum Critical Regime of the Unconventional Superconductor UTe 2
abstractText: The question of a possible quantum critical point lying inside of a superconducting phase is central for understanding unconventional superconductivity. In various unconventional superconductors, non-Fermi-liquid (with n < 2) or “strange-metal” (with n = 1) T n variations of the electrical resistivity have been identified as magnetic quantum critical phenomena. However, a difficulty is to prove experimentally that a T n variation identified at temperatures above the superconducting temperature is the signature of an intrinsic zero-temperature quantum critical regime. In the heavy-fermion paramagnet UTe 2 , unconventional superconductivity develops in the vicinity of a metamagnetic quantum phase transition induced by a magnetic field, and the quantum critical magnetic properties are suspected to play a role for the superconducting mechanism. In this work, we present a comparative analysis of electrical resistivity data collected on two UTe 2 samples of different qualities, in magnetic fields tilted by angles θ [Formula: see text] 35–40° from b to c. Fits to the data have been performed at temperatures higher than the superconducting temperature, either with a Fermi-liquid function ρ = ρ 0 + AT 2 or with a non-Fermi-liquid/“strange-metal” function ρ = ρ 0 + A n T n . Near to a superconducting phase induced beyond 40 T, T n fits lead to coefficients n [Formula: see text] 1. However, non-physical residual resistivities ρ 0 < 0 are also found, indicating that the T n laws cannot be extrapolated down to zero temperature. On the contrary, T 2 fits always lead to positive residual resistivities ρ 0 > 0, indicating — but not definitively proving — that they may extend down to zero-temperature in a virtual non-superconducting state. The results obtained here highlight the importance to investigate high-quality samples with low residual resistivity to confirm — or not — the presence of a suspected “hidden” quantum critical behavior masked by superconductivity.

title: Improving FMQA via Initial Training Data Design Considering Marginal Bit Coverage in One-Hot Encoding
abstractText: Factorization machine with quadratic-optimization annealing (FMQA) is a black-box optimization method that combines a factorization machine (FM) surrogate with search based on quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) by an Ising machine. When FMQA is applied to integer or discretized continuous variables via one-hot encoding, uniform random initial sampling can leave many binary variables never active in the initial training data, and the corresponding FM parameters receive no direct gradient updates from the observed responses. We address this by designing the initial training data to achieve complete marginal bit coverage, namely, ensuring that every binary variable obtained by one-hot encoding takes the value one at least once. We use two space-filling sampling methods, Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) and the Sobol’ sequence, yielding LHS-FMQA and Sobol’-FMQA. On the human-powered aircraft wing-shape optimization benchmark with 17 and 32 design variables, both proposed methods achieved numerically higher mean final cruising speeds than the baseline FMQA, with the advantage more pronounced on the 32-variable problem.

title: Scoping review of digital pathology for neoadjuvant rectal cancer response
abstractText: Aim: Neoadjuvant therapy for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) yields variable patient responses. Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital pathology offer a novel approach to preoperatively predict treatment outcomes using histomorphological features, potentially guiding organ-preserving strategies. This scoping review maps the current literature on AI-driven neoadjuvant response prediction in LARC to evaluate algorithmic performance and identify methodological gaps. Methods: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines, a structured search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was conducted for studies published within the last 10 years. Studies applying AI algorithms to pretreatment whole-slide images (WSIs) to predict neoadjuvant response in LARC were included. Results: Eleven publications were included. Ten studies used retrospective cohorts only, whereas one study also included a prospective validation cohort of 100 patients. Algorithmic frameworks predominantly featured classical machine learning, using software extraction of predefined features, and deep learning for autonomous pixel analysis. Across heterogeneous endpoints and cohorts, standalone classical machine-learning models reported external validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.811-0.908 (prospective: 0.733), a hybrid microenvironment model reported external AUCs of 0.643-0.656 (prospective: 0.630), and standalone deep-learning models reported an external AUC of 0.723 (internal: 0.710-0.81). Critical limitations across the field include heterogeneous clinical target endpoints, inconsistent baseline staging, and a reliance on “black box” algorithms lacking true biological explainability. Conclusion: AI-driven digital pathology demonstrates strong potential for predicting neoadjuvant treatment response in LARC. However, safe clinical implementation will require standardized endpoints, multimodal integration, and prospective multi-centre validation of algorithms anchored in verifiable tumour biology.

Lessons from the BEAT trial: implications for inhaled treprostinil from a double-blind, randomized trial
abstractText: Abstract Background Combination therapy is recommended for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), part of which generally includes prostanoids, which affect both the vascular tone and vessel remodeling seen in PAH. This study tested whether a dual prostacyclin treatment strategy (oral esuberaprost + inhaled treprostinil and oral background PAH therapies) would provide additional clinical benefit. Methods 271 World Health Organization functional class (FC) III/IV patients with PAH received placebo or 28.4 µg oral esuberaprost 4 times daily, in addition to newly initiated or ongoing inhaled treprostinil and background therapies. Results There was no difference between treatment groups in time to clinical worsening (primary endpoint); 49 (36.0%) patients on esuberaprost and 51 (37.8%) on placebo had a clinical worsening event. No favorable esuberaprost treatment effects were observed for the secondary or exploratory endpoints (6-minute walk distance [6MWD], Borg dyspnea score, and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP]). There were 21 all-cause deaths attributable to clinical worsening (esuberaprost: 8 [5.9%]; placebo: 13 [9.6%]). Post hoc exploratory analyses to investigate the effect of inhaled treprostinil on treprostinil-naïve patients ( n = 151) found that the addition of inhaled treprostinil was associated with improvements in multiple components of risk status, NT-proBNP, and 6MWD from screening through week 52, irrespective of background therapy. Notably, similar improvements were observed in patients on dual background therapy. Conclusion While the study did not meet its primary endpoint, the post hoc findings were consistent with current guideline recommendations to use multidimensional risk assessment when evaluating treatment response in PAH. title: Adenosine deaminase co-immunization reverses age‑associated immunosenescence by restoring germinal center T follicular helper cell function
abstractText: Abstract Older adults experience disproportionate morbidity and mortality from Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI); however, existing toxoid- and receptor binding domain (RBD)-based vaccines elicit suboptimal protection in aged hosts due to the age-associated defects in CD4 + T cell function, T follicular helper (T FH ) cell activation, and antibody quality. We evaluated whether adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzymatic immune modulator that degrades immunosuppressive adenosine, and improves GC T FH differentiation and survival, could reverse these age-related impairments when co-delivered with DNA vaccine plasmids targeting toxin A and B RBDs (pRBD). In aged mice, pRBD vaccination alone produced markedly reduced toxin-specific effector/memory CD4 + T cells, diminished T FH activation, and poor toxin A neutralization compared to vaccinated young mice. Co-immunization with plasmid-encoded adenosine deaminase-1 (pADA) restored toxin-specific CD4 + T cell generation and cytokine production, activation-induced marker (AIM) T FH responses, and antibody-mediate toxin neutralization to levels comparable to young adults. Mechanistically, pADA co-immunization was associated with the reduction of CXCR4 on germinal center (GC) T FH cells—an age-related defect linked to impaired GC positioning and diminished B cell help—suggesting that ADA improves humoral quality by correcting GC T FH mislocalization. These immune enhancements corresponded with improved clinical outcomes in morbidity, mortality, and weight-loss following C. difficile spore challenge of aged mice. Finally, pADA significantly reduced adenosine levels in aged lymph nodes, implicating a potential enzymatic-based regulation of GC immunosenescence. Together, these findings identify ADA as a metabolic adjuvant capable of reversing key features of vaccine immunosenescence and highlight adenosine dependent CXCR4 regulation as a tractable axis for improving vaccine efficacy in older populations.

title: Impact of cardiac phase selection on the diagnostic performance of CT-FFR: the role of myocardial bridging and heart rate
abstractText: Abstract Background Computed tomography-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) is a promising non-invasive tool, but the reliability of the conventionally preferred diastolic phase is challenged by high heart rates or myocardial bridging. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of systolic versus diastolic CT-FFR to identify the optimal reconstruction phase based on patient-specific characteristics. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 155 vessel segments from 138 patients with suspected coronary artery disease undergoing coronary CT angiography and invasive FFR. CT-FFR was calculated in diastolic and systolic phases. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed against invasive FFR (≤ 0.80 as positive), with stratified analyses for the FFR grey zone (0.75–0.85), myocardial bridging, and heart rate (≤ 70 vs > 70 beats per minute). Results Among 138 patients (mean age 65.4 ± 9.8 years; 91 men), diastolic CT-FFR demonstrated superior overall performance (AUC 0.91 vs 0.87; P = 0.021). In the FFR grey zone, systolic CT-FFR showed lower specificity (52.8% vs 77.8%; P < 0.05). In myocardial bridging patients, systolic CT-FFR had significantly lower AUC (0.79 vs 0.90; P = 0.011). In patients with heart rates > 70 bpm, systolic CT-FFR showed numerically higher but non-significant performance (AUC 0.87 vs 0.85; P = 0.418). Conclusions The optimal cardiac phase for CT-FFR is patient-dependent. While diastole remains superior for the general population and critical for patients with myocardial bridging or borderline lesions, the systolic phase may provide a viable alternative for patients with high heart rates when imaged on single-source CT platforms. An individualized cardiac phase-selection strategy is recommended to optimize the diagnostic accuracy of CT-FFR.

title: Bandedge-State-Limited Single-Photon Emission from Volumetric Quantum Design of 2D Colloidal Quantum Wells
abstractText: Abstract Present-day solution-processable single-photon sources are dominated by three-dimensionally confined colloidal quantum emitters, yet their particle-to-particle variation in single-exciton properties limits reproducibility and scalability. Here, to avoid such heterogeneity, we demonstrate reliable room-temperature single-photon emission from atomically flat two-dimensional (2D) colloidal quantum wells (CQWs) with inherently uniform one-dimensional quantum confinement, despite their long-standing limitations of efficient multiexciton emission and pronounced exciton-surface susceptibility. We resolve these challenges through volumetric quantum design (VQD) of CQWs, yielding a highly localized, single bandedge state. This design laterally confines the bandedge excitonic domain within the exciton coherent area and vertically decouples it from surface states via a thick, strain-relieved quantum-barrier shell that preserves strong confinement, overcoming the daunting thickness-confinement trade-off in 2D CQWs. Statistical single-particle spectroscopy reveals that VQD-CQWs deliver near-blinking-free (on-time: >99.5%) and fluence-insensitive antibunching (g(2)(0): ∼0.041), protected by a bandedge-state-filling bottleneck, together with linear polarization of up to 73% under cavity-free conditions, originating from synergistic transition-dipole and electric-field anisotropies. These advances establish 2D CQWs as a viable, homogeneous and scalable platform for quantum technologies.

title: A Koopman-PINN Framework for Epidemic Models: Parameter Inference and Forecasting
abstractText: We propose a Koopman-enhanced physics-informed neural network (K-PINN) framework for parameter inference and forecasting in nonlinear epidemic models. This method combines Koopman operator theory and physics-informed learning. It maps epidemic states into a latent observable space where the dynamics evolve approximately linearly while satisfying the governing epidemic equations through automatic differentiation. This integration improves interpretability, parameter identifiability, and long-term predictive stability. We apply the proposed framework to a normalized SEIRSD epidemic model and evaluate it using synthetic monkeypox (Mpox) data and real-world datasets from Germany, Morocco, and Sweden for the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Synthetic trajectories are generated using a structure-preserving, nonstandard finite difference scheme to ensure reliable training data. Numerical results demonstrate that K-PINN achieves more accurate parameter estimation, trajectory reconstruction, and long-term forecasting than classical PINNs and Koopman-EDMD approaches. These results suggest that K-PINN is an effective machine learning framework for epidemic modeling that can be extended to more complex systems.

title: Molecular Engineering of Customizable Resin-Derived Hard Carbon Framework for Efficient Sodium Storage
abstractText: Abstract Owing to their high carbon yield and molecular controllability, resins have emerged as promising precursors for hard carbon (HC) anodes in sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, achieving synergistic optimization of carbon microcrystals and sub-nanopores during resin pyrolysis to enhance sodium storage capacity remains a significant challenge. Herein, a spatial-chemistry-directed crosslinking (SCDC) strategy, based on the Mannich reaction of selected target molecules (TMs) within a resin network, is proposed. Owing to the steric hindrance of gem-dimethyl groups and the carboxyl-group-mediated interactions, the formation of nanoscale closed pores was facilitated while the continuity of sp2-hybridized carbon microcrystals was ensured and a large interlayer spacing was maintained. Through this approach, an HC architecture with elongated pseudo-graphitic domains and abundant closed pores is constructed in a synergistic manner, affording excellent electronic and ionic transport kinetics. The engineered HC exhibits an enhanced reversible capacity of 427.5 mAh g–1 and an outstanding initial coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 90.18%, along with a high reversible initial capacity of 346.7 mAh g–1 at 2 A g–1 and a capacity retention of up to 85.3% after 500 cycles. This study provides new insights into the microstructural design for high-capacity, high-rate sodium storage.

Adolescent social isolation and re-socialization increases alcohol intake and aversion-resistant drinking in male and female rats
abstractText: Abstract Rationale Adverse experiences during adolescence, especially social isolation, increases risk for alcohol use disorders (AUDs). Previous rodent studies of adolescent social isolation (ASI) encompassed all stages of adolescence and/or maintained isolation into adulthood, limiting identification of vulnerable stages of adolescence. Utilizing males only, or combining the sexes, also may have contributed to contradictory findings. Objectives Investigate social isolation restricted to discrete adolescent stages in combination with re-socialization and then persistent alcohol drinking. Determine whether adolescent isolation during specific developmental time periods, with or without subsequent re-socialization, leads to increased alcohol drinking in males or females. Methods Male and female Wistar rats underwent one of six housing conditions: (1) isolation from postnatal day (P)21–42 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Early), (2) isolation from P42–63 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Late), or (3) continuous isolation from P21 onward (ASI), or (4​–6) one of three appropriate control treatments. Alcohol-related behaviors were assessed in adulthood using intermittent-access two-bottle choice drinking (IAP), limited daily access (LDA-20) procedures, quinine-adulterated aversion-resistant drinking (ARD), and alcohol re-exposure following prolonged abstinence. Results In general, ASIR-Early and ASI elevated alcohol drinking in males and females, when compared to contemporary controls, during IAP, LDA-20, ARD, and after prolonged withdrawal, while ASIR-Late had largely similar effects as control conditions. However, for females, only ASI led to greater ARD at the highest quinine dose and also increased alcohol drinking after prolonged withdrawal. In contrast, for males, ASIR-Early and ASI had largely similar enhancement of alcohol drinking. Conclusions Under these conditions, isolation housing that encompassed the early adolescent period produced enduring increases in alcohol-related behaviors, with re-socialization perhaps more protective in females against ARD and elevated intake after abstinence. These results inform future studies that will investigate neural mechanisms underlying ASI-induced enhancement of alcohol drinking.

title: Firefly-Geni: Automated Iteration-Guided Generative Discovery of Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Molecules
abstractText: Abstract The efficient discovery of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) molecules remains heavily dependent on expert-driven design rules, while the vast structure–property knowledge accumulated in the literature stays largely fragmented and underutilized. Here, we present Firefly-Geni, an automated and interpretable active-evolution framework that transforms dispersed literature knowledge into structurally novel TADF candidates through a closed-loop workflow. Firefly-Geni integrates large-language-model (LLM)-assisted data extraction, multitask property prediction, conditional molecular generation, and theoretical evaluation. Its data-mining module converts unstructured literature into a curated database of experimental property entries. A dual-molecular-graph multitask predictor and a conditional generator are integrated with quantum-chemical feedback, enabling iterative refinement toward structural novelty. From 100,000 molecules generated under target conditions of a singlet–triplet energy gap ΔEST = 0.05 eV and a synthetic accessibility (SA) score of 2.5, Firefly-Geni identifies 100 structurally novel candidates computationally predicted to support reverse intersystem crossing and to be synthetically tractable, spanning diverse emission wavelengths. One synthesized candidate exhibited an experimental ΔEST of 0.019 eV and a film photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 84% under nitrogen, broadly consistent with the predicted small gap and high PLQY. Interpretability analyses further reveal chemically meaningful structure–property relationships and generation preferences, confirming that the candidates encode physically relevant low-ΔEST design motifs. This work offers a closed-loop, explainable strategy for actively evolving TADF candidates from literature knowledge, providing a generalizable route for data-driven molecular discovery.

title: Crystal Orientation Enables Near-Unity Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Resonant Metasurfaces
abstractText: Abstract Achieving near-unity nonlinear circular dichroism (CD) typically requires geometric symmetry breaking, making it challenging to combine helicity selectivity, resonant enhancement, and structural simplicity. We show that crystal orientation enables near-unity third-harmonic (TH) CD in highly symmetric resonant metasurfaces formed by a square lattice of circular holes in a cubic nonlinear material. Under circularly polarized excitation, strong near-field components of both helicities enabled by the rotational symmetry of the metasurface open two symmetry-allowed in-plane TH generation pathways. Crystal orientation controls their nonlinear coupling, selectively enabling destructive interference for one incident helicity. Our nonlinear temporal coupled-mode theory identifies the conditions for near-unity CD, reveals the distinct roles of pump and TH resonances, and explains the 4-fold and 8-fold crystal-orientation dependence. Across silicon, germanium, and diamond, we obtain resonantly enhanced TH CD exceeding 99% in the near-infrared, establishing crystal orientation as a design degree of freedom for nonlinear CD in highly symmetric metasurfaces.

abstractText: Abstract The accurate prediction of enzyme–substrate complex structures is challenging due to the transient and dynamic nature of these interactions. We evaluated the performance of eight machine–learning (ML) docking tools and the physics–based method AutoDock Vina as a reference in the prediction of enzyme–substrate complex structures using a curated data set of 210 diverse, non–redundant enzyme–substrate complexes, equally divided into three classes: metal–free enzymes (A), and enzymes with metal ions outside (B) or inside (C) the active site. All ML–based docking tools had low geometric accuracy and physical plausibility, with fewer than 10% hit rates at the stricter 2 Å threshold for substrate root-mean-square deviation. While no ML-based tools were able to outperform Vina in modeling physically plausible complexes, co–folding tools such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz–2 excelled at active–site localization, and many algorithms performed better for class C enzymes, and worse for class B enzymes. Surprisingly, DynamicBind, which was trained on less data with fewer parameters compared to other models, matched co-folding methods in active-site elucidation. Our results show that enzyme–substrate docking can be affected by the presence of a metal ion, and suggest that better performances for complex structure prediction may be achieved with data-centric strategies including molecular dynamics simulations rather than parameter-heavy ML architectures.

title: A deep learning and TOPSIS framework for predictive maintenance scheduling in smart manufacturing: an Industry 4.0 approach
abstractText: Abstract Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design. The scheduling evaluation demonstrates near-perfect discrimination, capturing all failure-proximate assets by targeting less than one-third of the fleet, with a 3.70-fold efficiency improvement over random allocation, an AUPRC of 0.9923, and tier discrimination significant at p < 10⁻¹¹. Cross-domain validation on CWRU Bearing Fault rotating machinery confirms perfect discrimination (AUPRC = 1.000) and a Spearman correlation of ρ = 0.803 between the closeness coefficient and physical fault severity, thereby supporting physically grounded scheduling without explicit severity supervision. These findings establish that coupling accurate deep-learning-based prognosis with principled multi-criteria decision-making yields high-confidence intervention decisions and quantifiable gains in resource efficiency in Industry 4.0 smart manufacturing environments.

Porogen-Assisted PLGA Nanoparticles Prepared by Emulsification–Diffusion as Candidate Nanoscale Ultrasound Contrast Agents
abstractText: Abstract Ultrasound imaging combined with ultrasound contrast agents (UCAs) has broad diagnostic applications. However, commercially available UCAs are typically micrometer-sized (1–8 µm), which largely confines them to the vascular compartment and limits their access to tumor interstitium. This study aimed to optimize the hydrodynamic diameter and in vitro echogenicity of hollow biodegradable poly(D,L-lactide-co-glycolide) nanoparticles (H-BPNPs) prepared by the emulsification–diffusion method using a three-factor, three-level Box–Behnken design. The independent variables were camphor amount (mg), stabilizer concentration (% w/v), and homogenization speed (rpm). The optimized H-BPNPs had a hydrodynamic diameter of 306.50 ± 2.09 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.05 ± 0.01, and a zeta potential of − 23.74 ± 0.23 mV. In vitro echogenicity studies showed that the optimized H-BPNPs produced greater mean grayscale value (MGV) enhancement than non-hollow PLGA nanoparticles (23.86 ± 0.63% vs 14.92 ± 0.58%). Scanning electron microscopy showed spherical particles, whereas differential scanning calorimetry indicated the absence of the camphor-associated thermal event after freeze-drying. Together with the increased echogenicity, these findings are consistent with the formation of low-density internal structures. The optimized H-BPNPs are promising candidates for further investigation as nanoscale UCAs; however, direct structural confirmation and in vivo validation are still required

title: Exercise Capacity and Mental Health in Adults With a Systemic Right Ventricle
abstractText: Background Adults with a systemic right ventricle (sRV) due to congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA) or atrial switch repair for d-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) experience substantial physiologic and psychosocial morbidity. Relationships among exercise capacity, sRV function, and mental health remain incompletely characterized. Objectives To characterize relationships among anatomic subtype, exercise capacity, sRV function, and mental health in adults with sRV physiology. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults with ccTGA or d-TGA (Mustard/Senning) followed at a tertiary Adult Congenital Heart Disease program from 2000 to 2025. Clinical, imaging, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, and patient-reported data were obtained from electronic health records. Mental health diagnoses were identified from clinical documentation. Functional status was assessed using NYHA class and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ-12). Results Among 137 adults (ccTGA, n = 51; d-TGA, n = 86), percent-predicted peak VO2 was lower in d-TGA than ccTGA (60% vs 74%, p < 0.001), as was sRV systolic function (41 ± 11% vs 47 ± 10%, p < 0.01). Anxiety or depression was more common in d-TGA (46% vs 25%, p < 0.05). Across the cohort, anxiety or depression was associated with lower exercise capacity, worse NYHA functional class, and lower KCCQ scores. Conclusions Adults with d-TGA following atrial switch have lower exercise capacity, reduced sRV systolic function, and greater mental health burden than adults with ccTGA. These findings support integrated assessment of physiologic performance, functional status, and mental health in adults with sRV physiology. Central Illustration. Integrated Cardio-Psychological Determinants of Exercise Capacity in Adults With a Systemic Right Ventricle. Adults with a sRV exhibit distinct clinical profiles according to anatomic subtype. Patients with d-TGA following atrial switch repair generally demonstrate lower exercise capacity, reduced systemic right ventricular systolic function, and a greater burden of anxiety, depression, and arrhythmias than patients with ccTGA. Exercise capacity reflects an integrated phenotype influenced by ventricular function, electrical disease, mental health, and functional health status. These findings support comprehensive assessment incorporating cardiac imaging, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, patient-reported health status, and mental health screening to guide multidisciplinary management and optimize functional performance and quality of life. Abbreviations: ccTGA = congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries; CMR = cardiac magnetic resonance; CPET = cardiopulmonary exercise testing; d-TGA = d-transposition of the great arteries; KCCQ = Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire; NYHA = New York Heart Association; sRV = systemic right ventricle; VO2 = peak oxygen consumption.

title: Detection of lipid-mediated diffuse pathological changes in multiple sclerosis: 7T feasibility study
abstractText: Background: Lipid dysregulation and myelin breakdown are hallmark features of multiple sclerosis (MS), yet current noninvasive biomarkers have limited sensitivity for detecting both focal demyelination and diffuse microstructural injury. We evaluated transient nuclear Overhauser effect (tNOE) MRI, a lipid-sensitive imaging technique, for mapping myelin-related alterations in MS. Methods: tNOE-MRI was performed in four MS patients and four healthy controls using a 7T scanner equipped with a 32-channel receive phased-array coil. Scan reproducibility was assessed across repeated sessions, and tNOE signal patterns were analyzed in major white-matter regions, including corpuscallosum and internal-capsule. Results: tNOE maps demonstrated strong contrast in highly myelinated structures, like splenium of corpuscallosum and internal-capsule. Inter-day and intra-day coefficients of variation were < 5%, indicating high measurement consistency. Quantitative analysis revealed that MS patients had significantly lower tNOE contrast in white-matter (12.6%vs16.1%) and grey-matter (5.9%vs7.2%) compared to healthy controls. The splenium exhibited the greatest tNOE reduction (~ 36%) in MS. Discussion: Reduced tNOE contrast corresponded with known regional differences in myelin density and suggests sensitivity to myelin-integrity. Lower tNOE signals in both white and gray matter indicate diffuse tissue alterations beyond focal lesions. With an acquisition time of ~ 3 minutes, tNOE-MRI shows promise as a rapid biomarker for MS diagnosis.

title: Eco-conscious synthesis of a starch-based magnetic hydrogel for effective methylene blue decontamination in wastewater treatment
abstractText: Abstract Novel magnetic hydrogels based on native Peruvian Amarilla Reyna potato starch were synthesized via radical copolymerization, followed by in situ co-precipitation of magnetite, nanoparticles for Methylene Blue (MB) removal from aqueous matrices. The materials were characterized by FTIR, XRD, SEM-EDS, VSM, swelling measurements, and pH PZC determination, confirming successful polymer grafting, a homogeneous Fe₃O₄ incorporation, magnetic recoverability, and a high swelling capacity (352.1 g/g). The magnetic hydrogel achieved a MB removal efficiency of 96% and an equilibrium adsorption capacity of 1148.3 mg/g at pH 10 and 30°C. Adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-first-order (PFO) kinetic model, reaching the equilibrium within 3 h, while the good fitting to the Langmuir isotherm model confirmed a monolayer adsorption behaviour. Thermodynamic analysis revealed that the adsorption process was spontaneous and exothermic, while Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations indicated a highly delocalized positive charge over the MB molecule, providing a molecular-level explanation for its weaker competition with small inorganic cations for negatively charged adsorption sites in complex aqueous matrices. Likewise, the hydrogel retained over 90% MB removal efficiency after five consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles, demonstrating an excellent reusability of the material. Tests in real water matrices showed a decreasing in the MB removal efficiency, c.a. 30-38%, due to ionic competition for the active sites and organic matter interference. The synthesized magnetic hydrogel demonstrated environmental safety, with no significant toxicity after treatment of the real effluents. These findings highlighted the potential of the obtained magnetic hydrogel as a sustainable and reusable adsorbent for dyes removal from complex aqueous matrices.

title: A-site Nd-doped LaBaCo2O5+δ perovskite oxide for electrocatalyzing hydrogen evolution reaction: experimental and theoretical studies
Therapeutic potential of SAT-3247 in a canine model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy
abstractText: Abstract Background Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked recessive disorder caused by the loss of functional dystrophin protein, resulting in progressive muscle degeneration in skeletal muscle due to myofiber fragility and muscle stem cell dysfunction. Satellos Biosciences developed an orally available small molecule SAT-3247 to promote repair and regeneration of injured skeletal muscle. SAT-3247 inhibits the kinase AAK1 to increase membrane localization of NUMB, resulting in enhanced polarity, increased numbers of asymmetric divisions, and increased generation of progenitors. Therefore, a pilot study was conducted with a mixed breed DMD canine model to explore the potential for SAT-3247 treatment to impact repair and regeneration of injured skeletal muscle. Case presentation: Two 9-month-old DMD dogs were treated for a period of 18 weeks, with oral delivery of SAT-3247 for 4 consecutive days per week (i.e., 3 days off) at 10 mg/kg dose. SAT-3247 treatment resulted in improved muscle morphology, decreased infiltration of inflammatory cells, increased regenerative index (measuring the ratio of regenerating to necrosing cells) in multiple muscles, improvement in locomotory parameters in both forelimb and hindlimbs including greater force generation, and stable cardiac function. Conclusions Overall, this proof-of-concept pilot study in a canine model highlights the therapeutic potential of SAT-3247 to repair and regenerate injured muscle and serve as a treatment for DMD. Together, these data provide a compelling preclinical groundwork for advancing SAT-3247 towards clinical evaluation in DMD patients.

title: Macrophage-associated mitochondrial transfer is linked to daunorubicin tolerance in AML models
abstractText: Abstract Interactions between acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) cells and the bone marrow microenvironment can reduce responses to chemotherapy. Macrophages are abundant in AML bone marrow, but how macrophage-associated mitochondrial trafficking relates to drug tolerance remains incompletely defined. Using AML cell lines, primary AML specimens and monocyte-, iPSC- and mouse bone marrow-derived macrophage models, we found that M-CSF-differentiated macrophages attenuated daunorubicin-induced AML apoptosis, with the strongest protection during direct co-culture. AML cells acquired macrophage-derived MitoTracker Deep Red signal, which increased with daunorubicin and was reduced by transwell separation, cytochalasin B and LIMK inhibition. Cross-species co-culture provided orthogonal molecular support through species-specific measurement of murine mitochondrial DNA, with murine nuclear DNA measured in parallel as a control. Macrophage co-culture was also associated with increased AML respiratory capacity and reduced reactive oxygen species. Exploratory proteomic analysis and interrogation of public transcriptomic datasets nominated RHOC/LIMK/cofilin signalling for follow-up, while TH-257 and metformin reduced the transfer-associated signal and macrophage chemoprotection. These findings support an association between acquisition of macrophage-derived mitochondrial material and daunorubicin tolerance in AML models and identify LIMK-dependent actin regulation as a candidate mechanism for further investigation.

title: Protocol to study bleomycin-induced skin fibrosis in mice
abstractText: Summary: Here, we present a protocol to model bleomycin-induced skin fibrosis in mice. We describe steps for inducing localized fibrosis using intradermal bleomycin administration and timed tissue harvest over 10 days. We then detail procedures to process tissues for single-cell RNA sequencing to quantify fibrotic progression and define cellular populations. This approach enables consistent induction of localized fibrosis for mechanistic and therapeutic studies. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Griffin et al. 1 Publisher’s note: Undertaking any experimental protocol requires adherence to local institutional guidelines for laboratory safety and ethics.

title: Tantangan Demokrasi dan Governance dalam Pelaksanaan Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG): Analisis Korupsi, Kesenjangan Sosial, dan Dominasi Elite
abstractText: Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) merupakan kebijakan publik nasional dengan anggaran besar dan banyak aktor, sehingga menimbulkan tantangan tata kelola, terutama kerentanan korupsi, kesenjangan sosial, dan potensi penguasaan kepentingan elite. Penelitian ini menganalisis tata kelola MBG dalam menghadapi ketiga persoalan tersebut melalui perspektif demokrasi, dengan prinsip Good Governance dan konsep Elite Capture sebagai kerangka analisis. Metode yang digunakan adalah kualitatif deskriptif dengan studi kepustakaan (library research) berbasis data sekunder dari jurnal ilmiah, buku, dokumen resmi pemerintah, laporan lembaga, dan pemberitaan media. Hasil menunjukkan kelemahan transparansi anggaran, akuntabilitas, pengadaan, dan pengawasan, termasuk dugaan penyimpangan yang masih diproses hukum dan belum berupa putusan berkekuatan hukum tetap. Konsentrasi kewenangan dan hubungan aktor politik dengan pengelola program membuka potensi Elite Capture, yakni penguasaan manfaat oleh kelompok tertentu. Perbedaan kondisi geografis, infrastruktur, dan kapasitas daerah berpotensi menghambat pemerataan manfaat, termasuk bagi kelompok rentan. Bagi masyarakat, MBG berpotensi meningkatkan gizi dan ekonomi lokal, tetapi kelemahan tata kelola mengancam keadilan sosial dan kepercayaan publik. Korupsi, dominasi elite, dan kesenjangan sosial tidak berdiri sendiri, tetapi saling berkaitan melalui lemahnya tata kelola dan ketimpangan akses terhadap sumber daya publik. Keberhasilan MBG tidak cukup dinilai dari besarnya anggaran, skala pelaksanaan, atau jumlah penerima manfaat, tetapi juga dari tata kelola yang transparan, akuntabel, partisipatif, dan berkeadilan serta kemampuan mencegah penguasaan kepentingan elite.

title: Analisis Penerapan Kurikulum Fiqih di Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Swasta Nurul Falah Yanfa Cadas
abstractText: Penelitian ini mengkaji implementasi kurikulum Fikih di Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Swasta (MIS) Nurul Falah Yanfa Cadas dengan memfokuskan pembahasan pada pelaksanaan Kurikulum Berbasis Cinta (KBC). Kajian ini berangkat dari perubahan kebijakan kurikulum yang sebelumnya menggunakan Kurikulum Merdeka menjadi Kurikulum Berbasis Cinta, yang berorientasi pada internalisasi nilai kasih sayang, penguatan karakter, serta penerapan prinsip-prinsip ajaran Islam dalam aktivitas keseharian peserta didik. Penelitian ini menerapkan metode deskriptif kualitatif dengan memperoleh data melalui wawancara bersama guru Fikih, yaitu Ibu Nadya Dwi Ananda, S.Pd. Berdasarkan hasil penelitian, diketahui bahwa kehadiran KBC tidak menyebabkan perubahan substansial terhadap cakupan materi Fikih, yang meliputi bersuci, salat, puasa, dan zakat. Perubahan lebih terlihat pada orientasi dan strategi pembelajaran yang diarahkan untuk menanamkan dimensi spiritual, membangun kepedulian sosial, serta meningkatkan tanggung jawab terhadap kelestarian lingkungan. Proses pembelajaran dikembangkan melalui kegiatan demonstrasi, latihan praktik ibadah, pembentukan kebiasaan positif, dan interaksi tanya jawab. Sementara itu, penilaian hasil belajar dilaksanakan melalui pemberian pertanyaan secara lisan, penyelesaian tugas tertulis, pengujian keterampilan ibadah, serta pemantauan perilaku peserta didik dalam keseharian. Dalam implementasinya, terdapat sejumlah hambatan, antara lain keberagaman tingkat penguasaan materi antarsiswa, kendala ketika melaksanakan praktik ibadah, alokasi waktu pembelajaran yang terbatas, serta kebutuhan untuk menanamkan nilai-nilai KBC secara konsisten dan berkesinambungan. Dengan demikian, penerapan Kurikulum Berbasis Cinta pada pembelajaran Fikih memberikan kontribusi terhadap peningkatan pengetahuan keagamaan, penguasaan praktik peribadatan, dan pembinaan akhlak peserta didik.

title: Penguatan Literasi Media dan Keterampilan Komunikasi Interpersonal bagi Anak Panti Asuhan Mutiara di Hative Besar, Kota Ambon
abstractText: Perkembangan teknologi informasi dan komunikasi memberikan kemudahan bagi masyarakat dalam mengakses dan menyebarkan informasi melalui media digital. Namun, kemudahan tersebut juga menghadirkan tantangan berupa penyebaran informasi hoaks serta rendahnya kemampuan sebagian pengguna media dalam mengidentifikasi dan mengevaluasi kebenaran informasi. Selain itu, keterampilan komunikasi interpersonal dan keberanian berbicara di depan umum merupakan aspek penting yang perlu dikembangkan sejak dini. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk memperkuat literasi media dan meningkatkan keterampilan komunikasi interpersonal anak-anak Panti Asuhan Mutiara di Hative Besar, Kota Ambon. Kegiatan dilaksanakan melalui pendekatan edukatif, interaktif, dan partisipatif dengan melibatkan 19 peserta dari total 27 anak panti yang berasal dari jenjang pendidikan SMP, SMA, hingga perguruan tinggi. Metode pelaksanaan meliputi tahap persiapan, pelaksanaan edukasi literasi media, permainan edukatif, latihan mini public speaking, serta evaluasi kegiatan. Materi literasi media difokuskan pada pengenalan informasi hoaks dan fakta, sedangkan penguatan kemampuan komunikasi dilakukan melalui diskusi, tanya jawab, permainan kelompok, dan latihan berbicara di depan umum. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa peserta mulai mampu mengenali karakteristik informasi hoaks, memahami pentingnya memeriksa kebenaran informasi sebelum menyebarkannya, serta menunjukkan partisipasi dan keberanian yang lebih baik dalam menyampaikan pendapat. Kegiatan ini memperlihatkan bahwa pendekatan edukasi partisipatif dapat menjadi salah satu upaya pemberdayaan anak panti asuhan dalam membangun sikap kritis terhadap media dan meningkatkan kepercayaan diri dalam berkomunikasi.

title: Menjembatani Jarak Bahasa: Strategi Mengatasi Hambatan Komunikasi dalam Pembelajaran Bahasa Arab
abstractText: Komunikasi yang efektif antara pendidik dan peserta didik menentukan keberhasilan pembelajaran, termasuk pembelajaran bahasa Arab. Namun, proses komunikasi di kelas kerap terhambat sehingga peserta didik sulit menguasai keterampilan berbahasa. Artikel ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi hambatan komunikasi dalam pembelajaran bahasa Arab dan merumuskan strategi untuk mengatasinya. Penelitian menggunakan metode tinjauan literatur dengan pendekatan deskriptif-kualitatif melalui penelaahan artikel jurnal, buku, dan penelitian terdahulu yang relevan. Hasil kajian menunjukkan delapan hambatan utama, yaitu kurangnya penguasaan mufradat, kesulitan memahami penjelasan guru, minimnya praktik berbicara, rasa malu dan tidak percaya diri, sikap merendahkan dari teman yang lebih mahir, lingkungan yang kurang mendukung, rendahnya motivasi dan dukungan orang tua, serta media pembelajaran yang kurang tepat. Hambatan tersebut memengaruhi keempat keterampilan berbahasa, terutama berbicara dan membaca. Enam strategi yang dirumuskan meliputi mengenali sasaran komunikasi, menyampaikan pesan secara jelas dan bertahap, memilih media yang tepat, membangun suasana yang aman dan empatik, memperbanyak praktik dengan umpan balik, serta menumbuhkan motivasi dengan melibatkan orang tua. Secara praktis, guru perlu memetakan kemampuan peserta didik, sekolah perlu menyediakan lingkungan berbahasa Arab, dan orang tua perlu mendukung kebiasaan belajar di rumah. Karena kajian ini bersifat konseptual, penelitian selanjutnya dapat menguji efektivitas strategi tersebut melalui penelitian tindakan kelas atau eksperimen.

title: Explaining perceptions of simulation in teacher education
abstractText: Simulation is established in many initial teacher education (ITE) programs in Australia, and implementations of specific platforms have been widely evaluated. This paper takes a broader approach by combining quantitative and qualitative data drawn from simulation surveys and course evaluation feedback representing students’ perspectives of three simulation platforms used in many courses over several years. Through this macro-level approach, it is possible to gauge overall sentiment and to identify core themes in the reasons students offer for their opinions. This is presented alongside staff perspectives, to consider the degree to which staff attitudes align with those of students. Collectively, the results of these analyses inform a two-dimensional framework based on the perceived verisimilitude of simulation platforms and the degree to which they require agency from users. This framework can serve as a tool to support the selection and placement of simulation platforms in terms of when and how they can be best integrated within programs to support practitioner development. A key element in this decision-making process is the recognition of a user’s stage of professional development, acknowledging that novice practitioners’ perceptions of and readiness for simulation vary depending on their level of expertise.

title: The Functional Duality of Agreed Payments for Non-Performance and a Unified Framework for Judicial Reduction - Focusing on the Interpretation and Issues for Further Consideration under Article 398 of the Proposed 2025 Amendment to the Korean Civil Act -
Designing through ambiguity: A postgraduate capstone for an uncertain digital society
abstractText: In a world of overlapping technological, environmental and social disruptions, higher education must move beyond transmitting knowledge towards cultivating the capacity to question, evaluate and respond under uncertainty. This conceptual paper presents the curriculum design of a 12-week postgraduate accounting capstone built around a pedagogy of ambiguity and supported by high-touch relational teaching. The curriculum combines contemporary topics such as AI acumen, media literacy, geopolitics and climate change with stable table-based groups, explicit teaching of active listening and brave conversations, repeated oral dialogue, weekly team submissions, community volunteering, and a professional identity storybook. A scaffolded five-stage framework is proposed to guide students to encounter ambiguity, interpret it together, create possibilities, articulate their thinking, and reflect on and reconstruct their professional identity. This conceptual curriculum-design paper proposes that when ambiguity is deliberately designed, modelled and supported through relational teaching, it can create the conditions for collaboration, creativity, confidence, and compassion in a changing digital society.

title: GenAI and novice programmers’ conceptual understanding: A systematic review
abstractText: Programming education remains challenging for novice learners, and the emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has introduced new opportunities and challenges for learning programming. While existing research reports a range of potential benefits, the influence of GenAI on conceptual understanding remains underexplored. This systematic literature review investigates the role of GenAI in influencing novice programmers’ conceptual understanding in higher education programming contexts. Guided by the PRISMA framework, empirical studies published between 2022 and 2026 were reviewed and synthesised using a conceptual understanding framework comprising three dimensions: understanding programming constructs, reasoning about program behaviour, and developing mental models of program execution. The findings indicate that GenAI primarily functions as a learning support tool that may enhance understanding of programming constructs. However, evidence is less conclusive regarding reasoning about program behaviour and is extremely limited in relation to mental models of program execution. The review suggests that the effects of GenAI are concentrated in more surface-level dimensions of understanding and do not consistently translate into deeper conceptual understanding. The study identifies important gaps in current research and outlines directions for further investigation.

title: Activating innovative learning environments: How educator pedagogical framings shape student- and human-centred learning
abstractText: Contemporary universities are increasingly investing in innovative learning environments (ILEs) to support student-centred approaches to learning and, more broadly, the aspirations of human-centred learning (HCL). While these environments are designed to promote collaboration, learner agency, and active participation, educators teaching in the same spaces often enact these pedagogical aspirations differently. This study examines how higher education educators interpret and activate the affordances of ILEs. Drawing on a constructivist, interpretive study, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 higher education educators who taught in replica ILE pilot spaces at an Australian university. Reflexive thematic analysis identified five interrelated continua representing pedagogical framings of teaching and learning: teacher as deliverer or facilitator, learner as recipient or agent, knowledge as transmitted or constructed, relationship as centralised or distributed authority, and student identity as generic or individual. Although participants consistently recognised the collaborative affordances of ILEs and expressed commitment to student-centred learning (SCL), the findings revealed two distinct enactments of SCL: one enacted for students and the other enacted with students. The study contributes an explanatory framework that suggests how the pedagogical potential of ILEs may be mediated not by spatial design alone, but by the pedagogical framings through which educators interpret and activate these environments.

title: Process flow and material balance of a waste-free technology for composite adhesive production from waste guanidine thiocyanate
abstractText: A three-stage batch technology for processing waste guanidine thiocyanate into a composite adhesive is proposed: precipitation of thiocyanate as copper(I) thiocyanate by copper(II) chloride in the presence of metallic copper, conversion of the guanidine hydrochloride into guanidinium polyacrylate, and preparation of a poly(vinyl alcohol)–colloidal silica adhesive. The stoichiometric material balance and the raw-material cost are given.

title: Self-care interventions to reduce, prevent or monitor disability in those affected by leprosy: a systematic review
abstractText: Abstract Background Self-care is a widely promoted strategy for the prevention and management of disability among people affected by leprosy. However, the content, delivery, and reported outcomes of self-care interventions have not been systematically analysed. This review aimed to identify and describe self-care interventions for people affected by leprosy, assess their outcomes, and map the interventions to the transtheoretical model of behaviour change. Methods A systematic review was conducted across PubMEd, Medline ALL, Web of Science Core Collection, EMBASE, LILACS, and SciELO. Studies were eligible if they reported a peer-reviewed self-care intervention for people affected by leprosy, including self-care interventions delivered within broader interventions. Data were extracted and formulated in an extraction table. Study quality was assessed using the relevant Critical Skills Appraisal Programme checklist. Findings were synthesised narratively. PROSPERO (CRD42025649623). Results Twenty-four studies were included. The studies were conducted in Brazil, Ethiopia, Nepal, Nigeria, China, India, Mozambique and Indonesia. Interventions included self-care or self-help groups; structured self-care education programmes and prevention of disability programmes; family-based or integrated disability-management interventions; assistive technology or adaptive devices; and tele-health interventions or follow-up. Foot-care was the most consistently reported intervention, and was most often linked to measurable outcomes, including ulcer healing and ulcer prevention. Hand-care and eye-care were more often embedded in larger broad self-care packages and did not report measurable outcomes. Evidence for ulcer impairment and prevention was promising but largely derived from uncontrolled non-randomised trials. Cost evidence for interventions was limited and no randomized control trials for self-care were identified. Conclusions This review shows that self-care interventions for people affected by leprosy may be effective in reducing disability, especially when they combine practical education, repeated follow-up, peer or family support, provisions of materials and devices, and access to wider health services. However, as shown by the review the evidence base remains limited by a lack of control trials and limited economic data. Future studies should use clearer intervention reporting, longer follow-up, and increased sample sizes to provide more evidence for which models are effective, sustainable, and transferable across leprosy endemic settings.

title: Acoustically optimized swarm of micro-drones in concert halls: from aeroacoustics to active acoustic masking
abstractText: This review paper examines recent advances in acoustic sensing, localization, noise mitigation, and decentralized swarm control of micro-drones operating in enclosed performance spaces, with a focus on concert-hall applications. We argue that an acoustically optimized swarm of micro-drones can act as a distributed, reconfigurable acoustic element of the hall itself (augmenting early reflections, masking residual self-noise, and providing real-time acoustic mapping) without permanent electroacoustic installations. We synthesize evidence from digital-twin-based adaptive concert halls, acoustic shells, onboard spectral analysis, acoustic localization systems (MicNest, AIM, GCC-PHAT arrays), acoustic drone-to-drone communication (HUM), passive and active noise reduction, and resource-constrained multi-robot formation control. We conclude that decentralized, AI-driven swarm control can sustain low-latency, reliable formation behavior on resource-constrained platforms in enclosed spaces, provided that localization accuracy, acoustic side-channel reliability, and perceptually motivated noise budgets are jointly engineered.

title: General practitioners’ experiences with pathology laboratory services and service disruptions in Aotearoa New Zealand: a qualitative study
abstractText: aims: The aim of this study was to assess general practitioners’ (GPs) knowledge about the medical laboratory landscape: how do they use laboratory services and what are their views on the strikes and current system? methods: Sixth year medical students conducted open-ended interviews with a convenience sample of 17 GPs using a protocol developed from the literature and discussion with a laboratory scientist. Interviews were recorded and transcribed. Transcripts were abductively coded. results: Four themes were identified: GPs were satisfied with their local laboratory service; there was variation in GP knowledge about laboratory structures; affected GPs struggled with the impact of the strikes but questioned whether there was significant public awareness of the strikes in among the various challenges in the healthcare system; laboratory service processes varied and GPs had many improvement suggestions. conclusions: GPs work closely with laboratories and value the relationships they have with skilled laboratory scientists. Current systems put pressure on laboratories’ ability to function effectively, which poses risks to equity, transparency and system resilience.

title: Teaching and assessing reflective writing in generative AI-mediated higher education: Vignettes and provocations
abstractText: This Pecha Kucha presentation offers a situated account of teaching and assessing in the evolving context of generative AI-mediated higher education. It aims to open up space for contemplation and dialogue around the complexities of the current teaching and learning landscape, where students and educators alike are grappling with new norms, and much grace and understanding needs to be extended on both sides as each learns from, and with, the other how to better navigate the complex nuances and permutations of AI-mediated academic work. Drawing on experiences from a postgraduate academic writing course that I teach, I share a selection of pedagogical vignettes and provocations emerging from my marking of the end-of-semester reflection assignments for the course. This assignment, requiring students to highlight key insights gained from the course and to reflect on these with reference to course discussions and their own scholarly practices, is one that I have greatly enjoyed marking over the years. However, vastly different patterns of engagement have been emerging from the students in recent semesters, and it seems evident that the affordances of generative AI, in changing how students tackle academic assignments, are at the same time disrupting some of higher education’s long-held assumptions about what constitutes learning, writing, and ownership. The pedagogical encounters highlighted include: students asking my own course chatbot to reflect on the course for them, reflections being flagged by AI-detection software as being potentially entirely AI-generated, diverse understandings regarding what constitutes one’s “own work” where AI has been used to assist in the writing process, and students unquestioningly accepting AI’s reformulations as “better” than their own (even when they were not). Encountering these has caused frustration, but I also see in these examples deeper epistemological and pedagogical tensions. Literacy scholars, particularly those working within an “Academic Literacies” perspective (e.g. Jones et al., 1999; Lea & Street, 1998; Lillis, 2003), have long argued that reading and writing are “social practices.” They are, in other words, situated within, influencing and being influenced by, the social and cultural contexts in which they take place. The educational landscape of today, with its myriad AI-assisted possibilities, raises questions of whether, how, and to what extent, our conceptions about “learning,” “writing,” and “ownership” may need recalibration. In fact, scholars have begun to recognise that current writing practices resulting in hybrid texts co-constructed by humans and AI are making it difficult, if not impossible, to identify distinct boundaries between AI-generated output and a student’s own intellectual efforts (e.g. Eaton, 2023; Wu et al., 2026). Higher education is in a season where excitement, curiosity, and unease about generative AI’s impact on academic work and learning sit in tension. Even as one who has actively sought to engage students in discussions of how we can productively and legitimately use generative AI in our writing, I found myself having unexpected reactions (of relief) when I encountered assignments with linguistic infelicities of the sort that suggested their writers had not used generative AI. The way forward, this presentation suggests, requires an intentional commitment to prioritise pedagogical approaches that foreground human connection – both in terms of cultivating a renewed intellectual and emotional connection of students with their own work, and in terms of building connection between students and instructors through open dialogue and compassionate, nuanced approaches to teaching and assessing.

title: Comparing the positive and negative impacts of AI: A large-scale study of student perspectives
abstractText: Higher education students are incorporating generative artificial intelligence into many aspects of their studies, yet the ways they judge its positive and negative impacts remain poorly understood. Using qualitative content analysis supported by code-frequency analysis, this paper examines open-ended comments from 2,802 participants drawn from a survey of 8,021 students across four Australian universities. Reported impacts clustered around four themes: study practices, quality, efficiency, and institutional practices. Positive impacts were more frequently coded overall, particularly when students described using AI to support their own study practices and efficiency. Negative responses centred on the inaccuracy of AI outputs. Although relatively few participants commented on institutional teaching and assessment practices, these responses were predominantly negative. The findings suggest that students value AI not only for the quality of its outputs, but also for its role in helping them begin, continue, refine, and complete academic work. Rather than uncritically accepting or categorically rejecting AI, students appeared to make situated judgements about its usefulness and limitations, shaped by concerns about accuracy and trust, as well as by the agency and control they retained over its use. Institutional responses should therefore engage with the complexity of students’ practices and the conditions under which they perceive AI to be useful or problematic.
